The provided text exhibits a strong reliance on end-rhyme and internal sonic repetition to create a cohesive auditory structure. The primary rhyme scheme is established in the first two lines, where "November" and "refrain" share a similar vowel sound (/eɪ/), creating a slant rhyme that binds the imagery of the storm to the concept of a mournful song. This is reinforced by the internal rhyme of "soaked" and "droplets," which, while not perfect rhymes, share the initial /d/ and /s/ consonant clusters, contributing to a sibilant and plosive texture that mimics the sound of rain.

The phrase "rhythmically descended" utilizes alliteration with the hard /d/ sound, emphasizing the downward motion of the rain. Similarly, "tapping out" employs plosive /t/ sounds to mimic the percussive nature of the raindrops. The word "morose" introduces a long /o/ sound that resonates with the somber tone of the "dreary night."

The final sentence, "Remind me the day that comes after 'Monday'?", breaks the poetic meter and rhyme scheme established in the previous lines. It shifts from a lyrical, descriptive mode to a direct interrogative, lacking the phonetic cohesion of the preceding text. The only sonic link is the repetition of the /m/ sound in "Remind" and "Monday," but this is insufficient to maintain the established poetic pattern. Thus, the text functions as a two-line poetic fragment followed by a prose-like question, with the phonological analysis primarily applicable to the first two lines.
